definitions.reconstruction: base feed answer * min(rate, cap ceiling) / 10**rate decimals, compared to the on-chain source answer
definitions.representable_fall: 1 - deepest floor bound translated into price units, divided by the current price
definitions.staleness_observability: whether the layer the protocol reads exposes a timestamp that a freshness check could inspect
definitions.test_1: can the oracle represent the stress and transmit it to the protocol

not_established: behaviour of any other Aave reserve or price source
behaviour at any block other than the pinned one
whether an operator would in fact pause or freeze in time
off-chain publication rules of the underlying feed
notes: A rejected update need not imply a failed read.
An aging round need not imply enforced rejection.
Heartbeat settings alone do not establish a freshness check.
Pauses and freezes require an operator transaction here.
The growth cap constrains the exchange rate, not the price.

caveats: the growth cap limits the exchange rate to 8.80% a year and currently has 2.91% of headroom; it is a ceiling on the ratio and does not constrain a fall in price
the protocol-facing layer exposes no timestamp, so no staleness threshold can be enforced against this price in code; freshness is an operational assumption, not an enforced condition
the deepest timestamp available is at base_feed, 2460 seconds before the pinned block, and is not read by this path
borrowing this asset is disabled, so a stale mark affects borrowing against it as collateral rather than borrowing it
reasons: the source answer is reproduced exactly from the base feed and the exchange rate, so the path is modelled, not assumed
no bound on the path prevents a fall of arbitrary size from being published, so a stress mark is representable
